study type: Secondary analysis of a Norwegian cohort study
exposure: Immigrant status (East, Southeast, and Central Asian, African, or Norwegian)
cohort: 10,125 low-risk pregnant women (Robson groups one and three) in Norway
finding: Immigrant women from East, Southeast, and Central Asia, as well as from Africa, had a higher risk of emergency cesarean section compared to Norwegian women.
mod_finding: Immigrant women from East, Southeast, and Central Asia, and from Africa had a higher risk of emergency cesarean section compared to women from the host country.
